# Changelog (US / English)

This file records the official evolution of the `FFX Project Editor` and the `Pt` workshop ecosystem.

It covers three levels of history:

- `main` releases and baselines;
- reconstructed semantic milestones for `main` from the pre-official-Git period;
- editorial mini-versions and knowledge snapshots for workshops `Pt2` through `Pt45`.

Rules for this changelog:

- **current rule (since 2026-06-04, see `docs/governance/VERSIONING.md` sec. 4):** every **shippable** addition (writer, module, proof, capability, registration doc) requires a bump in all four `FFXProjectEditor.csproj` version fields + an entry here **and** in `CHANGELOG.md` + a line in `VERSIONING.md`;
- classify each entry: **MINOR** / **PATCH** / **REVISION**; sign with lane ID (`Jarvis-ARENA`, `Jarvis-MAGIC`, etc.) when multiple chats run in parallel;
- keep the `[previous: vX.Y.Z.W]` chain linear â€” do not skip numbers;
- **no bump** for trivial only (typo, whitespace, internal rename, byte-identical refactor with no fix);
- also records milestones, relevant absorptions, freezes, blocks, and handoffs;
- does not fake old Git history that never existed;

### MINOR — release v2.245.1.0 integrated into the main branch

- **`v2.246.0.0` (2026-09-24, MINOR) — Controlled merge `release/v2.245.1.0` → `codexclaudiocodeffxeditor` with managed preview and Linux viewers restored.** Lane **Jarvis-DEVIN**. [previous: `v2.245.1.0`]
  - Controlled union of 334 files/22 conflicts: public Linux support (X11 + Skia backend), exact memory-lease NoClip overrides, release/allowlist contracts, audio tool payloads and server/route hardening — while preserving NoClip, Aurora, EditViewer and Monster AI authoring from the main branch.
  - Magic DLL Editor preview returns to the managed `MagicPreviewSession` flow (`?magicPreview={session}`, extracted DLL `.data` served under `/viewer-data/magic-preview/`): the `?magic=` path requires a vanilla `11/{id}.bin` the NoClip catalog never published for PC effects.
  - `ViewerHub.BuildUrl` gains a `forExternalBrowser` opt-in — Aurora Chamber/EditViewer, SceneRenderer, FieldExplorer, Magic preview and ViewerShell spin up loopback for the external browser on Linux (no WebView2); embed-only consumers stay gated. MonEditor builds the external URL lazily on click.
  - `ModuleDispatchRoute.Visibility` is computed per access, removing divergence between the static route table and `ModuleRegistry.Public` (`ai-assistant` gate). `Monster_Loot.Gil` has been `ushort` since the loot lane.
  - Validation: build 0 errors; focused Magic 48/48, dispatch/adapter/gate 28/28, viewer/MonEditor/Noclip/Aurora 960/960; broad suite ~2137 passing with failures confined to missing corpus (`FFX_TEST_MAGIC_CORPUS`/`FFX_TEST_MASTER_ROOT`). Verified visually on Linux: app launches and the managed preview opens NoClip in the external browser.
  - Integration recorded in `PORT_STATUS.md`. Merge commit `aac6665f`, follow-ups `7da3ba42` and `0594ba13`. Candidate, publication and RT2 are not promoted by this bump.

### PATCH — Monster AI Editor reliability

- **`v2.245.1.0` (2026-09-20, PATCH) — Protected persistence, numeric HP and consistent UI.** Lane **Jarvis-MonsterAI-Review**. [previous: `v2.245.0.0`]
  - Save/backup/restore preconditions, draft preservation and operand validation; the ATEL lab reloads applied AI. Invalid inputs and non-finite scale values are rejected.
  - Recipes use numeric HP/maxHP (`0/2`); percentage guards honor the selected threshold without I32 overflow. Lowest-HP targets use the correct opcode, with explicit legacy repair; complete guards survive reopening.
  - Closed models are no longer retained by the catalog event. Module-scoped contrast, accessible names and EN/PT UI text; dependency warnings use metadata instead of translated strings.
  - Includes the two images already referenced by the project, required for clean-checkout builds. This delivery does not promote RT2, publication or authoring capabilities outside existing contracts.
  - [Changes, validation and boundaries](docs/reverse/MONSTER_AI_EDITOR_FINISH_2026-09-20.md).

### MINOR — advanced ATEL authoring

- **`v2.245.0.0` (2026-09-20, MINOR) — Compound expressions and encounter scenes with bounded editing contracts.** Lane **Jarvis-ATEL-GAPS**. [previous: `v2.244.5.0`]

### PATCH — local ATEL correction

- **`v2.244.5.0` (2026-09-20, PATCH) — ATEL comparisons, arithmetic, and event editing aligned with the executable.** Lane **Jarvis-ATEL-CODEC**. [previous: `v2.244.4.126`]
  - Fixes `<=`/`>=` emission, both operand orders, phase condition reopening, and disassembler/Bible names. Unsigned comparisons retain uint32 semantics when edited; automation and SIN arithmetic checks now use `0x16=MUL`/`0x17=DIV`.
  - Event Explorer reads only the code region, validates call boundaries, and preserves successive patches; 123 native names verified and 397 events edited/restored byte-exactly. Integration into the development checkout: [JARVIS_ATEL_INTEGRATION_2026-09-20](docs/ai/handoff/JARVIS_ATEL_INTEGRATION_2026-09-20.md).
  - Direct binary verification, semantic regressions, corpus round trips, and evidence limits: [FFX_ATEL_CODEC_VALIDATION_2026-09-20](docs/reverse/FFX_ATEL_CODEC_VALIDATION_2026-09-20.md). Local delivery; no publication or new gameplay validation.

### REVISION
- **`[Unreleased]` (2026-08-15, REVISION) ? Encounter-zone map: IDA-proven `mapout.vpa` layout + variety-axis diagnosis.** Lane **Jarvis-MAGIC**. [bump to `v2.231.0.1` — coordinated commit pending, other-lane worktree dirty]
  - **Spatial-zone RE (IDA, canonical DB via ida-pro-mcp 13337):** cracked the real layout of `mapout.vpa` -> GuideMap root (`+6` n zones / `+10` n vertices / `+12` scale / `+24` vertex pool / `+28` zone pool). **Vertex = `s16 X,Y,Z` (stride 8)** (the offline parser read `X,Z` pairs, hence it failed on ~50+ fields; only bika03 matched). Zone record: `+8/+9` = `groupMin/groupMax`, `+6` n triangles, `+12` index ptr. Triangle = `i16 iA,iB,iC` + **meta dword `@+4`** -> **group `(meta>>17)&0x7FFF`** (IDA-proven, no `ordinal_guess`). Real blocker: `.vpa` is a **GS-DMA packet container** (magic 272); heavy geometry needs decoder `FFX_GS_ProcessDmaPacketData` (0x90f900), **not present in the project**; `ffxmap.id`/`mapobjdata.vpb` absent from the extracted corpus. Doc: `docs/reverse/FFX_MAPOUT_VPA_ZONES_RUNTIME_LAYOUT_RE_2026-08-15.md`; IDA comments applied (0x91d5e0/0x83e980/0x8447a0/0x909680).
  - **GrowLab finding:** 104 fails = 104 non-tight battles (0 in 588 tight) -> **lab false-negative**, not a writer bug.
  - **Variety axis (independent of the RE):** `EncounterTable_File.Rebuild()` GREEN — RT0 byte-identical + grow (+1 formation, +2B) on `btl.bin` (96 tables/192 groups/863 formations). BattleArenaAuthor add/remove monster byte-safe. Needs UI exposure (add formation + Rebuild-based save + danger).

### REVISION — 2.244.4.112
- **RE/doc: NODE16-RES — `req[]` = per-call `u32[8]` stack alloc or forwarded request pointer; field map: `req[5]`→`node+0x14`→ctxSlot, `req[6]`→`node+0x12`→scriptSlot, `req[7]`→`node+0x10`→workerIdx; residue gate @`0x86EA14`; `AiGoalCheck @0x86CA90` = full producer (immune by mechanism); most other producers leave `req[5..7]` uninitialized; requeue paths drop the binding fields → latent rebinding to residue; verdict: safe-by-luck, not proven-semantically-safe.** Devin subagent lane (NODE16-RES `bbdd1b26`) + fan-in **Jarvis-DEVIN** (2026-09-18). **Field map PROVEN (decompile evidence):** `req[]` is not a persistent object — it's the `u32 req[8]` stack-local the caller fills and passes to `Enqueue*`; the callee copies `req[5]`→`node+0x14`(ctxSlot), `req[6]`→`node+0x12`(scriptSlot), `req[7]`→`node+0x10`(workerIdx). The residue gate @`0x86EA14` checks `node+0x10`/`+0x12`/`+0x14` — if the caller didn't write `req[5..7]`, those fields receive **stack residue** from the previous caller. **Producer census:** `AiGoalCheck @0x86CA90` = the only full-producer (writes all 8 fields before enqueue) → immune by mechanism. All other non-menu producers (`AiGoalExec`, `BtlGoalExec`, `FieldGoalExec`, etc.) write only `req[0..4]` and leave `req[5..7]` uninitialized → **the node picks up residue**. **Requeue path:** `DequeueNode`/`RequeueNode` paths drop `+0x10/+0x12/+0x14` (only copy `+0x00..+0x0F` + the data fields) → after a requeue, the node loses the original binding and re-captures residue on next enqueue. **Honest verdict:** **safe-by-luck, not proven-safe** — the residue is benign by accident (the gate only fires on requeue + caller-without-write), not by mechanism. If a future caller crafts `req[5..7]` with adverse values, the node executes with arbitrary ctxSlot/scriptSlot/workerIdx → cross-context ATEL dispatch (modder trap, same family as the `epTable` OOB). **Deliverables:** `FFX_NODE16_RES_2026-09-18.md` + `node16_provenance.csv` (26 rows: function→producer-type→writes-req5-7→verdict) + `work/_node16res/apply_comments.py` (retry script for when MCP returns). **IDA pending:** `[w19-node16]` comments prepared but NOT applied (MCP dead) — re-run `python3 work/_node16res/apply_comments.py` when MCP is stable, then verify+`idb_save`. ### REVISION — 2.244.4.65
- **RE/doc+tool+PNG: FONT-ATLAS — the 3 FONT-SWIZZLE OPENs closed. Keystone: the PS2 `.fmt` pages are **dual-plane 4bpp atlases** — every cell holds TWO glyphs split by nibble *value* (`1–7`=even glyph id, `8–15`=odd glyph id); the HD remaster split the two planes into two RGBA pages.** Devin subagent lane (FONT-ATLAS) + fan-in **Jarvis-DEVIN** (2026-09-18). **Glyph-index→cell (PROVEN geometry):** `glyph g → cell (g>>1)`, `row=(g>>1)/12`, `col=(g>>1)%12`, `plane=g&1` (even→lo nibbles, odd→hi) — matches the runtime glyph-record formula `x0=14·((g%18)/2), y0=18·(g/18)` adapted to 10×12 cells. **`<F5:nn>` = slot5 = newkit** — a separate font (62 legal kanji; only 1/62 chars in sjistbl): it does **NOT** index this atlas (premise refuted honestly); the formula holds for the slot that binds TBP 15744 — prime candidate `uspc/menu/base.ftc` (metrics-only, 230 glyphs, slot4 confirmed via FTCX header byte+6). **`font_0_0` PS2 source (PROVEN):** = the **lo nibble-plane of the same `xfont1208.fmt`** (IoU 0.635, 178/252 cells >0.5); `font_0_1` = hi plane (IoU **0.889, 252/252 >0.5**) — the PS2 packs both HD pages in one 4bpp texture; **no separate file exists**. `jppc/menu/base.ftc` uses the same trick at 14×18 (999 glyphs, sjistbl 0–1007). **JP `subfont.fmt` variant (PROVEN census):** `uspc/subfont.fmt` = byte-copy of xfont1208; `jppc/subfont.fmt` differs in **32 cells** = heavier-weight redraws (katakana cells 6/64/65/79/82, fullwidth lowercase 117–129, ASCII-block lowercase 176–189; JP ink ≈2–3× US) — no extra pages, no charset change; a typographic locale revision matching the heavier JP main font. **Atlas block map:** cells 0–129 = JP block = `ffxsjistbl[0–259]` (cells 21–22 blank = undrawn circled-number slots → positional indexing PROVEN); 130–143 blank (kanji region); 144–191 = full ASCII at 10×12; 192–215 = 8-px-pitch compact ASCII (normal); 240–251 = same 8-px ASCII **bold**. **Deliverables:** `FFX_FONT_ATLAS_2026-09-18.md` + `data/wave14/font_atlas_{cells(252),charset(252),jpus_diff(32),hd_match(252),hypotheses(11)}.csv` + `data/font_atlas_2026-09-18/` (**14 proof PNGs**) + `research_tools/Ps2/font_atlas_decode.py` (stdlib+PIL). **Honest OPENs:** slot→block anchor binding (needs runtime page-code table), exact purpose of ASCII blocks B vs C (likely normal/bold), newkit's PS2 bitmap location (metrics-only on disc).   - **Discovery (source: noclip.website `src/FinalFantasyX/script.ts` â€” field-script opcode enum):** the codec mapping (`GT=0x0A, LT=0x0B, GE=0x0E, LE=0x0F`) was **inverted** vs noclip (`LT=0x0A, GT=0x0B...`). **Proven by decompile** of `FFX_Atel_InterpretWorkerOpcodes@0x864180` + `FFX_FieldVM_PopOperand@0x86DE90` (pop = top): with stack `[A(base), B(top)]`, **0x0B tests `A < B`, 0x0A tests `A <= B`** (0x0E/0x0F = float variants). **There is no direct "greater-than"** â€” the compiler expresses `A > B` as `[B, A] + 0x0B` (`B < A`). The log now emits `BLOB-PATCH2 #n ... write=0|1 safe=0xXX(how) risky=0xXX(how,ec=..)` (shows what it would do without writing) and, when opt-in + safe node, `BLOB-PATCH2 WROTE ...`. ## Historical Semantic Reconstruction

Important editorial note:

- the entries below record the historical ladder from `v0.1.0` to `v0.8.0-beta.1` as a consolidated reading of the project;
- they do not correspond to real old Git tags;
- they exist so we do not erase the fact that the editor was already much larger than a literal `v0.1.0` when Git officially entered the picture;
- the evidence used to build this ladder came from `PRODUCTION_V2_HANDOFF.md`, `FFX_PRIORITY_BUILD_MANIFEST.md`, `PORT_STATUS.md`, `PROJECT_HISTORY_MASTER.md`, `WORKSHOP_TIMELINE.md`, `PRODUCTION_ABSORPTION_MATRIX.md`, `PT_VERSIONING_REGISTRY.md`, and the workshop handoffs.

## [v0.8.0-beta.1] - historical reconstruction (pre-Git official SemVer)

Milestone where the ecosystem already operates as a large modular editor with multiple specialized fronts alive at the same time.

### Main Surface At This Stage
- `Monster Editor`;
- `Battle Explorer`;
- `Sphere Grid Explorer`;
- `Sphere Grid Editor v1`;
- `Encounter Table Explorer`;
- `Monster AI Explorer`;
- `String Explorer` with a safe `Monster Localizations` line;
- `Live Battle Lab`;
- a strong kernel line with `PlayerGrowthEditor`, `CtbBaseEditor`, and `MixTableEditor`.

### Ecosystem Pressure
- `Pt2 + Pt9` put `ModelViewerLab` on a serious recon and real handoff level;
- `Pt8` closes `Shop` as a guarded slice and honestly blocks `w_name.bin`;
- `Pt6` already dominates the `runtime + AI + proof` conversation;
- production already stops looking like â€œjust another editorâ€ and becomes a modding ecosystem far above the community baseline.

### Still Missing
- `ModelViewer v2` as a final viewport;
- proven `Repeat Exact Encounter`;
- `w_name.bin` writer;
- broad `btl_txt.bin` writer;
- clean integration of heavy runtime tooling.

## [v0.7.0] - historical reconstruction (pre-Git official SemVer)

Milestone where the main line shifts from â€œmore modulesâ€ to â€œmore proof.â€

### Added
- `BattleStructureLab` becomes the most technically heavy workshop of the old wave;
- `BattleRuntimeProbe`, sequencing watcher, and selector/bank narrowing enter the core conversation;
- `Force Battle / Repeat Encounter` stops being wishful thinking and starts being treated as a real observational experiment.

### Changed
- the official priority shifts toward `runtime + AI + proof`;
- production explicitly recognizes that encounter replay is still closer to `Repeat Route (Unsafe)` than `Exact Encounter`;
- the project's risk language hardens.

### Not Yet Safe
- blind `runtime/memory` merge;
- promotion of exact replay;
- brute port of the entire `Pt6` workshop into `main`.

## [v0.6.0] - historical reconstruction (pre-Git official SemVer)

Milestone where the kernel line and the conservative hardening of secondary systems stop being a promise and become part of a serious editor.

### Added
- `AutoAbilityEditor` matures as its own line with a conservative gate;
- `KeyItemEditor` enters the real absorption horizon;
- production already talks more cleanly to `Customization / Aeons` and other rebalance blocks.

### Changed
- port strategy stops being â€œcopy from the labâ€ and becomes â€œabsorb proven slicesâ€;
- obscure bytes such as `62h..67h` are kept `raw/read-only` instead of getting invented semantics;
- the kernel line stops being experimental and gains a harder editorial standard.

### Still Missing
- honest `Shop` writer;
- safe `w_name.bin`;
- runtime instrumentation strong enough for the next wave.

## [v0.5.0] - historical reconstruction (pre-Git official SemVer)

Milestone of the strong `KernelTablesLab` wave.

### Added
- `PlayerGrowthEditor`;
- `CtbBaseEditor`;
- `MixTableEditor`;
- mature `KeyItemEditor` line;
- early readiness for `Auto-Abilities`, `Item Shop / Gear Shop`, and `w_name.bin`.

### Changed
- the editor stops living only on battle/monster surfaces and gains a truly respectable kernel layer;
- a major part of rebalance modding becomes viable in its own UI;
- production gains a base for more curated future absorptions.

### Still Missing
- final production validation of `Auto-Abilities`;
- `Shop` as a conservative writer;
- reliable semantics for `w_name.bin`.

## [v0.4.0] - historical reconstruction (pre-Git official SemVer)

Milestone where the project learns to say â€œyesâ€ and â€œnoâ€ in text with real criteria.

### Added
- `TextRegressionHarness` as regression discipline;
- safe gate for `Name / Description`;
- safe gate for `Monster Localizations 1/2/3`;
- tooling that later becomes `TextLabTools` and `ProductionAuditTools`.

### Changed
- text formats previously called `Unsupported` in a generic way start being separated into:
  - `proven reader`;
  - `conservative writer`;
  - `blocked`;
- `Field String` and `btl_txt.bin` stop being romanticized as if they were â€œalmost ready.â€

### Still Missing
- broad `Battle Text` writer;
- honest `Field String` unlock;
- encode-safe handling for more obscure families.

## [v0.3.0] - historical reconstruction (pre-Git official SemVer)

Milestone where the editor stops being only a file browser and starts touching AI, runtime, and high-value gameplay surfaces.

### Added
- `Monster AI Explorer`;
- the first serious `Live Battle Lab` layers;
- stronger links between parser corpus, commands, forced actions, and live state;
- a better surface for encounter and script-behavior research.

- AI stops being a side topic and becomes a product priority;
- the idea of runtime proof becomes part of the editor's DNA;
- the project differentiates itself more clearly from the community by opening surfaces that almost nobody else offers.

- deeper turn-by-turn proof;

- exact encounter tooling.

## [v0.2.0] - historical reconstruction (pre-Git official SemVer)

Milestone of the editor's structural expansion into large visible systems.

- `Sphere Grid Explorer`;

- `Encounter Table Explorer`;
- stronger surfaces for battle structure and encounter tables.

### Changed
- the editor leaves the â€œa few strong domainsâ€ phase and becomes a tool with multiple large navigable areas;
- navigation between game domains becomes more coherent;
- the project gains real weight as a modding suite.

### Still Missing
- `Encounter Table Editor`;
- aggressive Sphere Grid topology work;
- deeper AI/runtime lines.

## [v0.1.0] - historical reconstruction (pre-Git official SemVer)

Honest minimum milestone where a real editor already existed, far above a disposable prototype.

### Added
- `Monster Editor`;
- `Battle Commands / Items / Monster Commands`;
- `Battle Explorer`;
- write-capable surfaces already real enough to characterize a product, not a mock.

### Changed
- the project starts existing as a usable editor even before any serious Git history;
- the main line already had its own identity and did not depend on â€œproof-of-conceptâ€ status to justify itself;
- this historical version is the point where it becomes fair to say that the `FFX Project Editor` was already an editor, even if still far from today's size.

### Still Missing
- editable `Sphere Grid`;
- dedicated encounter tooling;
- deeper AI/runtime;
- formal governance/versioning;
- the specialized workshop ecosystem.

## `v2.227.0.0` (2026-08-08) — Visual QA infra: opencode FREE models in `verboo_router.py` (honest limits + power comparison). **MINOR**. Lane **Jarvis-CLINE**. [previous: `v2.226.0.0`]
- **`scripts/verboo_router.py` — opencode free models:** new `OPENCODE_FREE_MODELS` dict (11 `oc/*-free`, limits observed on the gateway: ctx/maxOut/vision) + commands `free` (chat+vision via `-i`) and `freemodels`.
- **Honest opencode limits:** low ctx (131K–1M) and, crucially, a privacy warning — **free tier data is used to train the model**. Never send sensitive content.
- **Endpoint:** opencode free-tier gateway (`OPENCODE_FREE_BASE`), key `OPENCODE_FREE_API_KEY` or the `opencode.jsonc` fallback. Robust parser (JSON + SSE streaming, incl. `reasoning_details`).
- **Power comparison:** Verboo (unlimited tokens) stays default for heavy/common work; opencode free serves as a *second reference model* and simple tasks. Validated: `free` chat OK (deepseek-flash-free) and vision OK (mimo-v2.5-free described the screenshot; slower due to reasoning).

## `v2.226.0.0` (2026-08-08) — Visual QA infra: OpenCode Go integration (gpt-5.6-luna) + `desc` mode + humanized UX prompt + report fix. **MINOR**. Lane **Jarvis-CLINE**. [previous: `v2.225.2.0`]
- **`scripts/verboo_router.py` — OpenCode Go provider (new):** official endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`, 25 curated models (gpt-5.6-luna, deepseek-v4-pro/flash, glm-5.2/5.1, kimi-k2.x/k3, mimo-v2.5-pro, minimax-m3, qwen3.x, grok-4.5, hy3). New commands `ocg` (chat + vision via `-i`) and `ocgmodels`. `gpt-5.6-luna` uses the **Responses API** (`/responses`) — proven end-to-end accepting images (correctly described the FFX Mod Studio screenshot). Key from `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` or CLI auth fallback (`opencode-go`). Reserved for refined problems (reasoning/vision).
- **`qavisual` — model adjustment:** default is now `qwen3.6-27b` (structured tech/UX QA, JSON) — the only one that parses JSON in the real flow; new `--mode desc` uses `mimo-v2.5` in free prose (its natural use, no forced JSON). Cross-validation kept via `-m`.
- **Refined UX prompt (humanized):** `UX_PROMPT` rewritten for pragmatic human reading — new keys `o_que_esta_bom` (what is already good, don't touch) and `perfil_alvo`; the UX report renders these sections.
- **Markdown report fix:** 5 occurrences of `md += [list], ""` (tuple) broke `"\n".join(md)` with `TypeError` — `qa_report.md` was never generated. Fixed (bug reproduced and re-tested OK).
- **Fire test on the real editor:** captured the Menu (1616×1019) via `qa_capture.py --bring` + `qavisual --mode both`. Consensus: qwen parsed 2/2 (tech 7.5, ux 7.5), mimo 0/2 in JSON (confirmed: mimo is for free description). Also fixed the editor build (exe wouldn't open — `runtimeconfig.json` was missing from output; rebuild regenerated it).
## `v2.225.2.0` (2026-08-06) — F7 Monster AI Swap: status-on-ability via RAM. **MINOR**. Lane **Jarvis-HOOK**. [previous: `v2.225.1.0`]
- **`hooks/F7AiSwap.{h,cpp}` (new):** per-monster and per-ability (anim1 id), applies additional statuses TO THE TARGET when the monster uses that ability. All RAM (never edits bins). Config persisted to `modules/config/f7_aiswap.json` (atomic .tmp + MoveFileEx). Gate: `f7_aiswap.flag` / `FFXHOOKS_ENABLE_F7_AISWAP=1` (OFF by default).
- **Runtime (`F7_TickMainThread`):** edge detection on `Stat_action` (`+0xDD6`); when it changes and config matches (monsterId, anim1Id == action), applies status to the target (`Status_suffer` flags `+0x606` + turns `+0x608`). Logs `[ffx-hooks] AiSwap:`.
- **Menu F7 → Monster AI Swap:** now opens a submenu (was a raw opcode lever): Enable toggle, Configs, Reload from JSON, Save, Back. Routed via `ACT_AI_SWAP → F7_MENU_AI`.
- **Offset corrections vs plan:** the plan pointed `+0x641` as the status target field — that's `Status_resist` (immunity). Implemented on the correct field `Status_suffer`/`Status_suffer_turns_left` (source: `MemoryChr.cs`). The plan's 14-status table replaced by the real `StatusByteList` (25, Death=0..Slow=24).
- **Honesty:** `Stat_action`/`Seck_target_id` are documented HINTS (not causal truths); apply is flag-gated. **RT2 in-game pending** (field → battle → monster uses ability → target receives status).
- **Build PASS** (6.664→6.700 dllmain edits). Steam deploy (1.166.848 B). Example config: dingo(0x1009) with ability → Silence+Darkness and ability → Slow.


## `v2.225.1.0` (2026-08-06) — Treasure Map: ATEL header parse + glossary fix. **PATCH**. Lane **Jarvis-CLINE**. [prev: `v2.225.0.0`]
- **ROOT CAUSE of the 0-candidate treasure scanner:** `EventCallGlossary` had duplicate keys (0x0004/0x0005) throwing `TypeInitializationException` in the static ctor; the scanner's try/catch swallowed it so NO native call ever resolved a name. Fixed with a **duplicate-tolerant (last-wins)** build — `BuildEntries()` over a tuple list, preferring FFXDataParser ref-confirmed names.
- **ATEL header now parsed:** EV01 chunk 0 is an AiFile — `codeLen@0x00`, `scriptStart@0x30`, `workerCount@0x36`, worker-offset table@0x38. The scanner calls `DisassembleStructured(start: scriptStart, length: codeLen)` instead of disassembling from offset 0 (which included the header).
- **Accurate worker boundaries:** split now uses the header worker-offset table (fallback: STOP).
- **Proven result:** treasure scanner went from **0 to 338 candidates across 122 fields** (real `obtainTreasure` resolution).
- **Per-model world→guide divisor:** `ChestLocationIndexBuilder` uses `pos * LocalTransform.M11 / 10f` per YNGM model (real scale) instead of fixed `10f`.
- **Tests:** 4/4 TreasureMap + 71/71 Event/Atel/Glossary PASS.

- **RE (IDA GUI):** `obtainTreasure`(0x015B)→`FFX_Atel_Common_obtainTreasure@0x85A740` proven chest signature; speculative model ids 0x5002/0x50AA discarded; chest visual is engine-side (treasure slot table @0x1130F2F). `ConfirmedChestCandidates` went from 0 to 338 (criterion: TreasureIds.Count>0). Doc: `docs/reverse/TREASURE_CHEST_RE_VALIDATION_2026-08-06.md`.
- **Treasure Map editor (UX/polish + bug):** chest list per field now shows the **real takara.bin reward** (`RewardText` via `TreasureRewardLookup.Describe`, 333/338 resolve); **visual fallback** (placeholder at map bounds) for chests without a recovered position; **cached** `ChestLocationIndexBuilder` (no longer rebuilds every field's projections on each selection); **latent bug fixed** — chests now projected with the SAME canvas projection (`_rProj`) instead of fixed 900x700 PixelX/Y, keeping alignment with geometry at any canvas size. New test `TreasureRewardDescribeTests`.
- **Fix (routing):** Treasure Map module would not open (click did nothing) because the `case "treasure-map"` was missing from `Main_Window.Dispatch` — it was registered in `ModuleCatalogPolicy` but had no handler. Added `case` + `MenuItem_TreasureMap` (standard `SetModule`), + namespace `using`. Opens normally now.
- **Treasure Map editor (RT2 feedback fixes):** (1) edit panel was not truly editable — `SelectedReward` was never initialized (empty/"hidden" Reward combo) and `Save` did not apply row edits; now initializes with the current value (match EncodedId==Type, 304/338 + Gil=29; 5 rare key-items stay null) and persists via `TreasureChestRow.ToEditedRecord()` on Save/Discard; (2) reward picker hidden for Gil (`SelectedRewardVisible`); (3) Center button now centers placeholders (chests without a real position); (4) multi-state navigation renamed to "Map state n/m" and chevrons hidden when single-state. Tests: `Most_Chest_Rewards_Resolve_To_Picker` + `Edit_Record_RoundTrips_Through_Writer` (RT0).
